text:
Fraser Minten has 8 goals in 23 games for Boston, already close to half his career total, and the 22-year-old center has earned a real role, playing just over 16 minutes a night.

The finishing is running hot. He's scoring on 17.8% of his shots against a talent range that tops out near 17%, and his 8 goals come from 5.6 expected. The Bruins have also scored about 6.5 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. Strip out the luck and you have a solid middle-six center, which is still a nice return on a second-round pick Toronto traded away.

The worry is at 5-on-5, where Boston gets outshot with him on the ice and does about 8 points of expected goal share worse than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking gives him one clear skill: he carries the puck in on 60% of his entries. Our range has him at 17 to 27 goals, a good season even if the shooting cools.
